    03 THE PURPOSE

    One question.
    Many ways in.

    Consciousness is studied across disciplines, traditions, and scales. No single map can settle the question.

    Noemorph brings records and their citations into one browsable collection. It is designed to help curious readers find their bearings, follow a source, and see where a claim begins and ends.

    This is a collection in progress—not a finished synthesis or a claim to completeness. Inclusion of a position is not endorsement.

    04 OUR APPROACH

    A map with
    its edges showing.

    Good research makes its sources visible and its uncertainties legible. These are the principles behind the collection.

    01 / TRACE

    Follow the source.

    Each record points to retained citations, with source roles and verification states where available. A recorded locator is a starting point, not proof that a source supports every claim.

    02 / DISTINGUISH

    Keep differences intact.

    Scientific theories, philosophical positions, lived traditions, constructs, and clinical models are separately typed rather than treated as interchangeable theories.

    03 / QUESTION

    Leave room for review.

    The collection has no fixed denominator. Relationships between ideas remain locked until the coverage protocol and independent review are complete.

    05 THE COLLECTION

    Explore the atlas.

    Start with a question, a name, or a discipline. Open a record to examine its description, limits, and citations, then share it or export its references.

    ✳

    A note on interpretation. Records are provisional research entries. Citation locators and DOI resolution do not by themselves verify that a source supports a claim. Non-consensus positions are included for study, not endorsement.

    More filters

    Citation filters find records with at least one citation in that state. They do not verify all claims in a record.
